notes: PRINTED-APPENDIX SPECIFICATION (Nov 4, 2026): outside the main-text sample (PROTOCOL 5b ruling (r)); for the appendix-inclusive sensitivity analysis. Retail-to-Online Access design (gvar online_treat_time), CEM-matched sample of Appendix Table C.3 column (2) and Figures C.1-C.2 (Retail-to-Online panels). Matching: same matchit() call on rto_county_matching_info.csv, code.R lines 815-836; the estimation sample is rto_main_subset == T rows of the matched counties (code.R line 834), re-run with generate_results() and the usual weights; matching weights (all 1) are never used, so this is a 1:1 matched sample restriction (PROTOCOL 5b). sample_filter = rto_main_subset plus the 422 matched counties (211 eventually online, 211 retail-only; article: '211 (out of 1,077) ... and 211 (out of 498) control counties'), reproduced with MatchIt 4.7.2; the matched set reproduces all 12 printed matched-sample entries of Appendix Table C.2 to 4 decimals. Sample: 422 counties, quarters 9-30, 5,425 rows (unbalanced: 419 counties enter after quarter 9); 10 adoption cohorts (quarters 12,14,15,16,18,21,23,25,27,29); 211 never-online counties (47.5% of rows); no always-treated counties. Event study: authors' aggte(type = 'dynamic', min_e = -8, max_e = 16) with varying base period; pipeline uses universal base period (identical post-period coefficients, pre-period coefficients differ in definition); same bins, reference and summaries as the main-text template. The figure prints no coefficients: published_coef is null and authors_rerun_coef holds the authors' dynamic overall ATT (e = 0..16), the quantity the pipeline's CSA post-average targets. Authors report Callaway-Sant'Anna with the main-text settings (code.R generate_results(), lines 277-364: did::att_gt, control_group = 'notyettreated', est_method = 'dr', base_period = 'varying', allow_unbalanced_panel = TRUE, xformla = ~1, weightsname = 'num_individs_2015', clustervars = county, bstrap = TRUE without a seed; aggte(type = 'simple' or 'dynamic', min_e = -8, max_e = 16)). No TWFE regression exists in the package; the TWFE counterpart is D = 1[gvar > 0 & time >= gvar] with county FE + quarter FE, weights num_individs_2015, clustered by county. Treatment never switches off (defined from a unit-constant timing variable). Outcome levels were additively transformed by the authors to hide actual levels (README); county IDs anonymized; underlying UC Consumer Credit Panel is restricted. Project member Davide Proserpio is a coauthor (PROTOCOL Section 6). CAVEAT: the sample is an unbalanced panel with counties entering at their state's retail launch; did with allow_unbalanced_panel = TRUE uses repeated-cross-section 2x2 cells whose control composition changes between g-1 and t, which drives the authors' and the pipeline's CSA estimates (see the replication log, 'composition-driven' section). TWFE and BJS are unaffected.

event_structure.source: code.R line 237 (did::att_gt, control_group notyettreated, est_method dr, base_period varying, allow_unbalanced_panel TRUE, weights num_individs_2015, cluster county) and generate_results() (aggte type 'dynamic', min_e = -8, max_e = 16), applied to the CEM samples at code.R lines 809 and 907 and plotted at lines 920-925 (Appendix Figures C.1-C.2); article Section 5: 'event studies and ATTs covering 8 quarters before and 16 quarters after the policy'. Event time e = time - online_treat_time (quarters); time is consecutive in the sample (9..30), so e = rel = t - g in the pipeline index. Callaway-Sant'Anna path: single-quarter bins -8..16 as reported, reference -1 (universal base; the authors' varying base changes only the pre-period definition). Relative times outside the window get open endpoint bins (<= -9, >= 17), estimated but not summarized, so no treated row is uncovered: did keeps those rows and computes their cells (early pre-periods of late cohorts are not-yet-treated controls for earlier cohorts), so 'drop' would change the published path, and pooling them with the reference would subtract their effects from every CS bin. No authors' TWFE exists; the TWFE counterpart estimates the same bins.
